Definition: from G4052; surplusage, i.e. superabundance:--abundance(-ant, (-ly)), superfluity.
BiblicalUsage: Perisseia is abundance, surplus, superfluity. In a great trial of affliction the abundance of the Macedonians' joy and their deep poverty abounded to liberality, and James tells us to lay apart all superfluity of naughtiness and receive the engrafted word.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that abundance is proved by what it gives: deep poverty abounded to riches of liberality, and the superfluity of naughtiness must be laid aside.
